The *Kammavipākaja Sutta* (Ud 3.1; PTS Ud 21) is a discourse in the *Udāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts a monk who meditates while experiencing severe bodily pain engendered by past kamma, yet endures it mindfully without being broken by it, occasioning an inspired utterance from the Buddha [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists sixteen modern translations in thirteen languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary reference passages in the dossier address this sutta, as occurrences of the term *kammavipākaja* in the search results relate instead to doctrinal analyses of illness (such as in the *Sīvaka Sutta*) or commentarial categories of psychic power (*iddhi*).

Verse parallels to the sutta are preserved across several recensions of the *Udānavarga* in the *Bhikṣuvarga* chapter, including Sanskrit versions (UV 32, UVS 32), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 32), and Chinese translations in the Taishō canon (T 212.33 and T 213.32) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 70 text-reuse matches shared between Ud 3.1 and fourteen other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Udāna*, its most extensive shared passages occur with the *Mahāmoggallāna Sutta* (Ud 3.5, 5 matches across 702 characters, aligning §2.1_0–4.1 with §1.4–3.1), the *Taṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (Ud 7.6, 6 matches), the *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 4.7, 5 matches), and the *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10, 4 matches), alongside stock phrases shared with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 6) and *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 7 and SN 54) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records a cross-language alignment with the Sanskrit *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* (score 85), which reflects generic opening phrasing (§0.1–1.1) rather than a direct textual parallel [DharmaNexus].
